description: Comprehensive provenance registry for microgravity, normal gravity, and Quasi-2D/2D flame spread constants across backend/fire_model.py, backend/materials.py, ai/surrogate.py, and main.py.

categories.category_2: Calibration & Empirical Microgravity Flame Spread Constants

uncertainty_semantics.ensemble_disagreement: Standard deviation across 5 surrogate models. Represents epistemic uncertainty (model disagreement), NOT real-world error.
uncertainty_semantics.physics_uncertainty: First-order Taylor series error propagation (Kline & McClintock, 1953 / ISO GUM) combining input measurement tolerances (O2 +-1.5%, flow +-5%, thickness +-2%, pressure +-1%) with applicability-scaled model-form uncertainty.
uncertainty_semantics.confidence_interval_multiplier: 1.96 x std under Gaussian assumption (95% CI). Does NOT include systematic physics error.
uncertainty_semantics.applicability_score: Continuous distance-based heuristic score (0-100) aligned with NASA-STD-7009A V&V credibility envelopes. Higher score = closer to Saffire I-VI / BASS-II flight-validated envelope.
uncertainty_semantics.caveat: In-sample calibration against 13 Saffire/BASS flight points (2.83% core MAPE, 5.90% combined MAPE); leave-one-out out-of-sample MAPE 4.15% (core 5) and 6.68% (all 13). NOTE: ROD_CURVATURE_*, LOW_P_RAD_FEEDBACK_EXP and THERMAL_DEPTH_* / THIN_THICK_RATIO_* were tuned on the full 13-point set and are NOT refit inside LOO, so LOO is optimistic for them.

T_AMBIENT_K.derivation: Standard reference ambient temperature (25.0 C / 298.15 K) for standard-state thermodynamic and transport property evaluations.

PRESSURE_REF_KPA.derivation: Standard sea-level atmospheric pressure (1 atm = 101.325 kPa), baseline for NASA terrestrial testing and nominal ISS baseline atmosphere.
PRESSURE_REF_KPA.reference: NASA-STD-3001 Vol 2; CODATA / IUPAC STP conventions

X_O2_AIR.derivation: Dry sea-level atmospheric oxygen mole fraction used as standard baseline oxidizer concentration.

NU_AIR_300K.derivation: Kinematic viscosity of air at ~300 K and 101.3 kPa (nu = mu/rho, approx 1.846e-5 m^2/s).
NU_AIR_300K.reference: Incropera & DeWitt, Fundamentals of Heat and Mass Transfer, Appendix A (Air properties at 300 K)

K_AIR_300K.derivation: Thermal conductivity of dry air at 300 K (k approx 0.0263 W/(m K)).
K_AIR_300K.reference: Incropera & DeWitt, Fundamentals of Heat and Mass Transfer, Table A.4

gas_conductivity_temp_exp.derivation: Power-law temperature scaling of gas thermal conductivity, k_g = K_AIR_300K * (T_eff / 300.0)^0.7. Standard approximation for air across combustion boundary layers.
gas_conductivity_temp_exp.reference: Standard power-law gas transport approximation; no specific single-paper citation.

X_REF_M.derivation: Characteristic reference boundary layer / sample width scale (10 mm) for non-dimensional Reynolds and Grashof evaluations. NOTE: This is a conventional choice, not a uniquely derived constant. Different reference lengths would change non-dimensional numbers but not physical behavior.
X_REF_M.reference: Fernandez-Pello, A. C. (1995), 'The Solid Fuel Microgravity Flame Spread', Prog. Energy Combust. Sci.

CONFIDENCE_Z_95.derivation: Two-tailed critical Z-score for 95% confidence interval under Gaussian assumption.
CONFIDENCE_Z_95.usage_note: Used ONLY as 95% CI multiplier for ensemble disagreement (std x 1.96). NOT a real-world uncertainty estimate. See uncertainty_semantics block.
CONFIDENCE_Z_95.reference: NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook of Statistical Methods, Section 1.3.5.7

T_FLAME_MAX_K.derivation: Effective flame temperature ceiling (not true adiabatic) for near-limit microgravity diffusion burning of cellulosic/acrylic polymers prior to radiative extinction. Represents the effective reaction-zone temperature including radiative losses.
T_FLAME_MAX_K.reference: Urban, D. L. et al. (2019), Saffire-I/II Final Reports, NASA NTRS; typical values for diffusion flames in reduced gravity range 1600-2000 K.

MICROGRAVITY_THRESHOLD_G.derivation: Operational boundary (1e-2 g0) below which buoyant convection velocities fall below typical forced ventilation levels, making buoyancy negligible relative to diffusive/forced flow.
MICROGRAVITY_THRESHOLD_G.reference: NASA microgravity science operational definitions; Saffire experiment operations guidelines

QUIESCENT_FLOW_CMS.derivation: Critical lower air velocity limit below which excessive radiative heat loss extinguishes microgravity flames due to insufficient convective oxygen supply (radiative quench boundary).
QUIESCENT_FLOW_CMS.reference: Derived from Saffire-I and BASS-II low-flow radiative quench observations (NASA NTRS). Exact paper volume/DOI pending verification.

FLOW_STRAIN_CRITICAL_CMS.derivation: Onset threshold where aerodynamic stretch and reduced residence time in the gas-phase reaction zone induce convective flame stabilization strain.
FLOW_STRAIN_CRITICAL_CMS.reference: Saffire flow-velocity sweep results (S5/S6 sample analysis) - exact paper citation pending verification against published strain-rate curves.

BLOWOFF_FLOW_CMS.derivation: Critical cross-flow blow-off limit where flow residence time is shorter than chemical reaction induction time (Damkohler extinction limit, Da < Da_c).
BLOWOFF_FLOW_CMS.reference: Saffire-IV/V/VI extinction datasets; Ruff, G. A. et al., 'Large-scale fire safety tests aboard Cygnus', NASA TM - exact value pending verification against published blow-off curves.

L_PH_THIN_BASELINE_M.derivation: Characteristic thermal preheat length parameter (7.8 mm) for thin SIBAL fuel when explicit Stefan-Boltzmann solid surface radiative cooling (q_surf = eps*sigma*(T_pyro^4 - T_inf^4)) is included in the net heat flux balance, restoring exact Saffire-I S2 flight parity (1.343 mm/s).
L_PH_THIN_BASELINE_M.reference: Olson, S. L., Ferkul, P. V., et al., 'Flame spread: Effects of microgravity and scale', Combustion and Flame, Vol. 199, January 2019, pp. 168-182. DOI: 10.1016/j.combustflame.2018.10.012 - theoretical framework from Fernandez-Pello, A. C. (1995), Prog. Energy Combust. Sci.

F_CONCURRENT_THIN_MICROG.derivation: Flight ratio of concurrent-to-opposed flame spread rate over thin SIBAL fabric in low-velocity microgravity, computed from Saffire-I Sample 1 (concurrent, v_f approx 0.224 mm/s) and Sample 2 (opposed, v_f approx 1.343 mm/s), yielding 0.224 / 1.343 = 0.1668 approx 0.165.
F_CONCURRENT_THIN_MICROG.reference: Olson, S. L., Ferkul, P. V., et al., 'Flame spread: Effects of microgravity and scale', Combustion and Flame, Vol. 199, January 2019, pp. 168-182. DOI: 10.1016/j.combustflame.2018.10.012 - Saffire-I S1 (concurrent, v_f approx 0.224 mm/s) and S2 (opposed, v_f approx 1.343 mm/s) reported in this paper.

F_CONCURRENT_THICK_MICROG.derivation: Ratio of microgravity concurrent to opposed flame spread for thick PMMA (10 mm), order-of-magnitude estimate from Saffire-II multi-sample data where boundary-layer detachment slows concurrent advance.
F_CONCURRENT_THICK_MICROG.reference: Saffire-II summary report (2018), NASA Glenn Research Center. Order-of-magnitude estimate pending tighter calibration.

F_CONCURRENT_THIN_BUOYANT.derivation: Upward (concurrent) to downward (opposed) flame spread ratio under normal gravity (1g) for thin cellulosic fuels. Buoyancy preheats unburned fuel ahead of the flame front.
F_CONCURRENT_THIN_BUOYANT.reference: Fernandez-Pello & Hirano, 'Controlling Mechanisms of Flame Spread', Combust. Sci. Tech. 32 (1983); Quintiere, J. G., Fundamentals of Fire Phenomena, Wiley (2006)

F_CONCURRENT_THICK_BUOYANT.derivation: Upward to downward flame spread ratio for thick polymers (e.g., PMMA) in 1g. Buoyant turbulent flame plume bathes solid fuel, driving rapid radiative/convective preheating.
F_CONCURRENT_THICK_BUOYANT.reference: de Ris, J. (1969), 'Spread of a Laminar Diffusion Flame', 12th Int. Symp. Combust.; Quintiere, J. G., 'A theoretical basis for flammability metric', Fire and Materials (2002)

LOI_MICROG_FACTOR_DEFAULT.derivation: Reduction factor for Limiting Oxygen Index (LOI) in microgravity (LOI_ug approx 0.85 x LOI_1g). Absence of buoyant convective cooling allows materials to sustain burn at lower ambient O2 concentrations under low forced flow.
LOI_MICROG_FACTOR_DEFAULT.reference: Semi-empirical reduction factor based on BASS-II microgravity vs. normal-gravity flammability limit observations (NASA NTRS). Exact citation pending verification.

flame_temp_o2_scaling_exp.derivation: Sub-linear exponent scaling flame temperature with oxygen mole fraction (T_f proportional to (X_O2)^0.42), capturing non-stoichiometric dissociation and radiative damping at elevated oxygen levels. Semi-empirical fit, NOT a rigorous theoretical value.
flame_temp_o2_scaling_exp.reference: Calibrated against NASA-STD-6001B flammability test atmospheric sweeps; theoretical grounding in Glassman & Yetter, Combustion (4th ed.). Specific exponent value is this model's empirical fit.

flame_temp_pressure_term.derivation: Dimensionless pressure-scaling pre-factor accounting for three-body collision recombination reactions and radical pool concentrations at higher total pressures. Semi-empirical.
flame_temp_pressure_term.reference: Empirical fit; theoretical grounding in Kashiwagi, T. et al., 'Combustion of Solids under Variable Pressure', Combust. Flame (1990)

flame_temp_pressure_exp.derivation: Pressure exponent (P^0.25) matching observed flame temperature and reaction-zone density changes over spacecraft exploration pressures (approx 50 to 101 kPa). Semi-empirical.
flame_temp_pressure_exp.reference: NASA/CR-2005-213600; Hirsch, D. et al., 'Flammability of Materials in Sub-Atmospheric Enriched Environments'

loi_pressure_correction_exp.derivation: Pressure sensitivity coefficient adjusting fuel flammability threshold (LOI(P) = LOI_ref x (P_ref/P)^0.12), reflecting increased flammability at lower total pressure with elevated O2.
loi_pressure_correction_exp.reference: NASA-STD-6001B Test 1 Flammability Database; Hirsch, D. et al., 'Pressure and Oxygen Effects on Upward Flame Spread', J. ASTM Int. (2010)

RAD_LOSS_COEFF_MICROG.derivation: Radiation loss fraction at 1 atm. Scales linearly with pressure (gas-phase emission coefficient proportional to molecular density). At lower pressure, fewer emitting molecules, so less radiative loss, so higher net heat flux to fuel. Verified against Saffire-V S4 (55 kPa, 28% O2) flight data.
RAD_LOSS_COEFF_MICROG.reference: T'ien, J. S. et al., 'Mechanisms of Flame Spread and Smolder in Microgravity', NASA SP-2003-212054; Saffire infrared radiometer package data.

radiation_loss_1g.derivation: Fraction of heat release emitted as radiation (approx 15%) for small-scale buoyant turbulent/laminar flames under standard Earth gravity.
radiation_loss_1g.reference: SFPE Handbook of Fire Protection Engineering (5th ed.), Chapter 2: Heat Release Rates; Quintiere (2006)

char_k_eff_factor.derivation: Effective thermal conductivity ratio (k_char / k_virgin = 0.65) for insulating porous pyrolyzed carbonaceous char layers in thermosets, phenolic, and natural polymers.
char_k_eff_factor.reference: Moghtaderi, B. et al., 'Thermal Properties of Charring Materials at Elevated Temperatures', Combust. Sci. Tech. 130 (1997); NASA TP-3540

strain_exponent_thin.derivation: Empirical strain damping power-law exponent for thin thermally-thin fuels subject to forced aerodynamic convective flow (u^0.58), reflecting thermal boundary layer thinning. Fit from Saffire thin-fuel cross-flow response curves.
strain_exponent_thin.reference: Olson, S. L., Ferkul, P. V., et al., 'Flame spread: Effects of microgravity and scale', Combustion and Flame, Vol. 199, January 2019, pp. 168-182. DOI: 10.1016/j.combustflame.2018.10.012 - Saffire-I/III thin-fuel cross-flow response curves.

STRAIN_EXPONENT_THICK.derivation: Aerodynamic strain damping exponent for thermally thick fuels (u^1.35), where both gas-phase flame length and solid-phase conductive heat penetration are aerodynamically attenuated. Fit from Saffire thick-fuel flow sweeps.
STRAIN_EXPONENT_THICK.reference: Saffire-II PMMA slab flow-parameter sweeps; Urban, D. L., et al., 48th ICES Conference (2018) - Saffire-II flow-duct measurements. Value 1.35 is this model's empirical fit, not directly published as a single number.

l_ph_thick_boundary_factor.derivation: Theoretical ratio of conductive preheat length to hydrodynamic boundary layer thickness (delta_th / delta approx 0.63) derived from classical de Ris thermally-thick flame spread formulation.
l_ph_thick_boundary_factor.reference: de Ris, J., 'Spread of a Laminar Diffusion Flame', 12th International Symposium on Combustion (1969), pp. 241-252; Sirignano, W. A. (1972)

qnet_extinction_threshold.derivation: Minimum net surface heat flux required to sustain pyrolysis. Below 1 W/m^2, energy budget cannot support steady fuel vaporization (radiative quench boundary).
qnet_extinction_threshold.reference: Standard pyrolysis energy balance; verify against Saffire post-extinction data.

uncertainty_fixed_pct_in_range.derivation: Baseline relative epistemic/aleatoric error bound (20%) applied when ALL inputs fall inside the flight-validated envelope. Conservative placeholder pending real-data MAPE calibration.
uncertainty_fixed_pct_in_range.reference: Validation RMSE of Saffire-I through Saffire-IV spread-rate measurements against 1D/2D numerical models (NASA/CR-2020-220491). To be replaced with actual MAPE when holdout data available.

uncertainty_fixed_pct_out_of_range.derivation: Elevated relative error bound (40%) applied when ANY input falls outside the flight-validated envelope. Reflects extrapolation uncertainty.
uncertainty_fixed_pct_out_of_range.reference: Engineering judgment for extrapolation; documented as HEURISTIC not calibrated.

regression_rate_proxy.derivation: Nominal mass burning regression rate proxy (2% of spread rate) for charring and non-charring polymers under low-flow microgravity. ILLUSTRATIVE - used in transient simulation to keep thickness_remaining from being constant.
regression_rate_proxy.reference: BASS PMMA burning regression observations (order-of-magnitude); exact value pending tighter calibration against Saffire thickness/time data.

width_correction_reference_mm.derivation: Sample width above which no narrow-width correction is applied: (200 / width)^0.15 for width < 200 mm.
width_correction_reference_mm.reference: BASS-II narrow sample vs Saffire wide sample data.

width_correction_exponent.derivation: Empirical power-law exponent for narrow sample width correction. Flame spread increases as sample width decreases due to edge heating. Fit to BASS-II narrow sample (50 mm) vs Saffire wide sample (410 mm) flight data. Semi-empirical, pending full 2D formulation.
width_correction_exponent.reference: BASS-II narrow sample observations vs Saffire wide sample data.

rod_geometry_factor.derivation: Cylindrical curvature heat-focus multiplier (1.85x) paired with 1.18x radial diffusive O2 entrainment (effective combined ~2.18x), preventing double-counting on BASS-II PMMA rod experiments.

low_flow_thin_fuel_threshold_cms.derivation: Flow below which thin-fuel spread gets the enhancement boost (5 / flow)^0.15.

low_flow_thin_fuel_exponent.derivation: Empirical power-law exponent for low-flow enhancement of thin fuel spread. Below 5 cm/s, boundary layer thickens and radiative preheating increases relative to forced convection, accelerating spread. Fit to BASS-II B1 (3 cm/s) data.

near_loi_margin_threshold.derivation: Relative O2 margin above effective LOI below which flame spread is ramped down. Heuristic.
near_loi_margin_threshold.reference: Calibrated against Saffire-IV S2 (26% O2) only; no published source.

near_loi_exponent.derivation: Exponent of the near-LOI slowdown: factor = (margin / 0.15)^1.5.
near_loi_exponent.reference: Calibrated against Saffire-IV S2 only; no published source.

near_loi_floor.derivation: Minimum multiplier of the near-LOI slowdown, so spread never drops below 10% of the unscaled value.

min_regression_rate_floor.derivation: Numerical and physical non-zero floor to prevent singularity in burn-duration calculation near flame extinction boundaries.

THIN_FUEL_THRESHOLD_M.derivation: Biot number boundary criterion dividing thermally-thin (Bi < 0.1, d <= 1.0 mm) and thermally-thick (Bi > 1.0, d > 1.0 mm) solid fuel regimes for cellulose and PMMA.
THIN_FUEL_THRESHOLD_M.reference: Drysdale, D., An Introduction to Fire Dynamics (3rd ed.), Wiley; Fernandez-Pello (1995)

MIN_FLOW_FLOOR.derivation: Safety floor in V_forced = max(flow/100, 0.001) - prevents divide-by-zero in aerodynamic strain calculations.

MIN_PRESSURE_RATIO_FLOOR.derivation: Floor in p_ratio = max(pressure / P_ref, 0.05) - prevents unrealistic exponential blowup at near-vacuum conditions.

MIN_DT_PYRO_FLOOR.derivation: Floor in dT_pyro = max(T_pyro - T_inf, 50.0) - prevents divide-by-zero for materials with near-ambient pyrolysis temperature.

MIN_DELTA_F_FLOOR.derivation: Floor in max(delta_f, 1e-4) - prevents divide-by-zero in convective heat flux when boundary layer is ultra-thin.

MIN_NU_G_FLOOR.derivation: Floor in max(p_ratio, 0.1) when computing kinematic viscosity - prevents unphysical viscosity blowup at near-vacuum.

DEFAULT_LOI_VALUE.derivation: Fallback LOI applied when a material is missing the LOI field in the materials database. Typical for commodity polymers.

MIN_CHUNK_LEN_RAG.derivation: Minimum semantic character threshold below which segmented document fragments lack sufficient context for dense vector embedding.

CHUNK_SIZE_RAG.derivation: Chunk size targeting aerospace material datasheet sections and combustion paper paragraphs without truncating context.

CHUNK_OVERLAP_RAG.derivation: Standard approx 20% chunk-boundary overlap window to preserve cross-sentence semantic continuity for technical equations and citations.
CHUNK_OVERLAP_RAG.reference: Lewis, P. et al., 'Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks', NeurIPS (2020)

physics_ai_sanity_threshold.derivation: Guardrail tolerance (30% relative discrepancy): if surrogate output deviates by >30% from first-principles physics, surrogate is flagged as out-of-distribution and system falls back to physics engine.

PENALTY_MATERIAL_NOT_VALIDATED.derivation: Heavy deduction when material is not in the Saffire/BASS flight-validated list (CORE_NASA_NAMES). Physics extrapolates to unvalidated materials, carrying higher uncertainty.

PENALTY_GRAVITY_OUT_OF_RANGE.derivation: Applied when gravity level is outside validated range [0, 1] g. Values above 1g or below 0g are extrapolations beyond flight data.

PENALTY_O2_OUT_OF_RANGE.derivation: Applied when ambient oxygen falls outside validated range [12%, 30%] - the NASA-STD-6001B spacecraft cabin flammability-test bounds.

PENALTY_FLOW_OUT_OF_RANGE.derivation: Applied when forced flow falls outside validated range [0.5, 30] cm/s - the Saffire ventilation regime.

PENALTY_THICKNESS_OUT_OF_RANGE.derivation: Applied when fuel thickness is outside validated range [0.1, 15] mm - covers SIBAL fabric through thick PMMA slabs.

SCORE_THRESHOLD_HIGH_CONFIDENCE.derivation: Minimum score for HIGH applicability categorization - prediction lies within flight-validated envelope.

SCORE_THRESHOLD_MODERATE_CONFIDENCE.derivation: Minimum score for MODERATE applicability; scores below this flag predictions as LOW / out-of-distribution.

STEFAN_BOLTZMANN.derivation: Exact CODATA 2018 Stefan-Boltzmann constant for solid surface radiative heat loss q_surf = epsilon * sigma * (T_pyro^4 - T_inf^4).
STEFAN_BOLTZMANN.reference: CODATA 2018; Bhattacharjee et al. (1996), ASME J. Heat Transfer 118(1), 181-190

surface_emissivity_default.derivation: Fallback hemispherical infrared surface emissivity when material-specific emissivity is not specified; category-specific values (0.35-0.95) defined in backend/materials.py.
surface_emissivity_default.reference: Incropera & DeWitt (2007), Fundamentals of Heat and Mass Transfer, Table A.11

soot_radiative_feedback_coeff.derivation: Luminous flame soot radiative feedback augmentation factor at elevated oxygen mole fractions (X_O2 > 0.21).
soot_radiative_feedback_coeff.reference: Quintiere, J. G. (2006), Fundamentals of Fire Phenomena, Ch. 10

quasi2d_lateral_o2_entrainment_coeff.derivation: Lateral diffusive oxygen enrichment scaling factor (1 + 0.35 * min(delta_f / W, 0.6)) for finite-width sheets with free edges.
quasi2d_lateral_o2_entrainment_coeff.reference: Olson, Ferkul & T'ien (1988), 22nd Symp. Combust.; BASS-II narrow-sample edge-diffusion observations

quasi2d_clamped_edge_conduction_factor.derivation: Characteristic lateral conductive heat sink coefficient (4 * k_s * tau * dT_pyro / W^2) modeling quenching width behavior in conductive metal sample holders.
quasi2d_clamped_edge_conduction_factor.reference: Quintiere, J. G. (2006), Fundamentals of Fire Phenomena, Ch. 7 (Critical quenching width)

thin_thick_smoothstep_bounds_m.derivation: C1-continuous cubic Hermite transition interval [0.5 mm, 2.0 mm] around nominal 1.0 mm thermal thickness boundary to eliminate unphysical step discontinuities.

sphere_geometry_factor.derivation: 3D spherical curvature heat-focus multiplier for spherical PMMA fuel specimens tested in BASS-II microgravity experiments.
sphere_geometry_factor.reference: BASS-II PMMA sphere microgravity flame spread dataset

pde_2d_fourier_cfl_limit.derivation: Explicit 2D Von Neumann / Fourier stability criterion Fo = alpha_s * sub_dt / min(dx^2, dy^2) <= 0.20 governing automatic sub-stepping in simulate_2d().
pde_2d_fourier_cfl_limit.reference: Patankar, S. V. (1980), Numerical Heat Transfer and Fluid Flow

FLOW_STRAIN_CRITICAL_THIN_CMS.derivation: Aerodynamic strain onset threshold for thermally thin fabrics in microgravity (30 cm/s), calibrated to Saffire-I/III 20-25 cm/s flow-sweep data.
FLOW_STRAIN_CRITICAL_THIN_CMS.reference: Olson, S. L., Ferkul, P. V., et al. (2019), Combustion and Flame, 199, 168-182

ROD_CURVATURE_BASE.derivation: Cylindrical speed-up at delta_f/D -> 0. Fitted to BASS-II B5 (6.35 mm) and B9 (9.5 mm); 2 parameters on 2 points, zero degrees of freedom.

ROD_CURVATURE_SLOPE.derivation: Growth of rod speed-up with delta_f/D (capped at ROD_CURVATURE_RATIO_MAX=1.5). Fitted jointly with ROD_CURVATURE_BASE.

LOW_P_RAD_FEEDBACK_EXP.derivation: Sub-atmospheric multiplier (P_ref/P)^n on flame radiative feedback. Chosen from S4 (55 kPa, 28% O2) alone; single-point calibration, not derived from Bhattacharjee et al. 1996.

THERMAL_DEPTH_COEFF.derivation: Empirical solid thermal depth delta_th = C*alpha_s*V_eff^-0.25 (V_eff in m/s). Dimensionally ad hoc; chosen so SIBAL/Nomex stay thin while 0.8 mm PMMA trends thick.
THERMAL_DEPTH_COEFF.reference: Empirical; MIST_04, Saffire-IV S2, SIBAL points

THERMAL_DEPTH_V_EXP.derivation: Velocity exponent in empirical thermal depth.

THIN_THICK_RATIO_LO.derivation: tau/delta_th below which fuel is fully thin (was 0.75).

THIN_THICK_RATIO_HI.derivation: tau/delta_th above which fuel is fully thick (was 1.80). Results for 0.8 mm PMMA are knife-edge sensitive to these edges (1.7% to 172% error for +-0.05 shifts).

NASA_SMAC_CO_1H_PPM.derivation: NASA 1-hour Spacecraft Maximum Allowable Concentration (SMAC) for Carbon Monoxide in habitable spacecraft modules.
NASA_SMAC_CO_1H_PPM.reference: NASA JSC 20584, Spacecraft Maximum Allowable Concentrations for Airborne Contaminants

NASA_SMAC_HCN_1H_PPM.derivation: NASA 1-hour SMAC ceiling for Hydrogen Cyanide (mitochondrial cytochrome c oxidase inhibitor).
NASA_SMAC_HCN_1H_PPM.reference: NASA JSC 20584, Spacecraft Maximum Allowable Concentrations for Airborne Contaminants

MICROG_INCOMPLETE_COMBUSTION_MULTIPLIER.derivation: Enhancement factor for CO and soot yields under buoyancy-free microgravity diffusion burning due to oxygen starvation.
MICROG_INCOMPLETE_COMBUSTION_MULTIPLIER.reference: T'ien et al. (2003), NASA SP-2003-212054; Olson et al. (2019), Combust. Flame 199

PBA_O2_COHB_WASHOUT_HALF_LIFE_MIN.derivation: Elimination half-life of Carboxyhemoglobin (COHb) under 100% normobaric oxygen therapy (Portable Breathing Apparatus), vs ~320 min on room air.
PBA_O2_COHB_WASHOUT_HALF_LIFE_MIN.reference: Weaver, L. K. (2009), Carbon Monoxide Poisoning, New England Journal of Medicine, 360(12), 1217-1225
